summary: Two macOS DiagnosticReports for BOOHTACORD 1.0.15 record the same EXC_BAD_ACCESS/SIGSEGV at address 0x40 in FlutterRTCVideoRenderer's queued first-frame callback. The callback dereferenced an ivar through weakSelf after the renderer could have been disposed. A nil guard is covered by a test-first source regression, all 17 flutter_webrtc tests pass, the macOS Debug build compiles, and a live Pixel-to-Mac full-screen share rendered the complete portrait frame and stopped cleanly without a crash.

checks.name: Repeated macOS crash signature
checks.observation: BOOHTACORD-2026-09-30-212149.ips and BOOHTACORD-2026-09-30-214429.ips both report EXC_BAD_ACCESS/SIGSEGV, fault address 0x40, on the main queue in __39-[FlutterRTCVideoRenderer renderFrame:]_block_invoke_2. Both reports identify bundle ru.boohtacord.boohtacordDesktop version 1.0.15.

checks.name: Regression test before fix
checks.observation: The new focused test failed before the implementation change because the queued callback did not guard a disposed renderer.

checks.name: flutter_webrtc package tests after fix
checks.observation: All 17 package tests passed, including the macOS renderer lifecycle regression and the source parity check for the shared Darwin/macOS implementations.

checks.name: macOS Debug native compilation
checks.observation: The Debug app built successfully with the guarded Objective-C renderer callback.

checks.name: Post-fix Pixel-to-Mac live screen-share retest
checks.observation: Pixel 7 (Android 17/API 37, BOOHTACORD 1.0.15+20, account microphone muted) shared the entire screen in SHARE_TEST to the macOS Debug client (1.0.15+20, microphone muted). Both clients showed the two-person roster and approximately 5–6 ms RTT. The Mac participant card exposed the share and opened the viewer; after the first frames arrived, the complete portrait display—including its top and bottom edges—was visible with side letterboxing and no crop. The Mac client remained responsive without crashing. Stopping the share on Android returned the Mac viewer to the roster and removed the share.

remaining: This closes the macOS renderer crash retest only. Windows parity, Android OS-level stop, repeated reconnect/stop cycles, and broader screen-share acceptance remain open in the platform checklist.
